They explicitly distinguish 'autonomous commerce' (AI across enterprise operations) from 'agentic shopping' (AI acting for customers), and claim Sphere powers over $100 billion in annualized GMV.
competitor_cards.why_it_matters: This is category-creation, not incremental positioning. commercetools is attempting to define the next era of commerce infrastructure the way they defined 'headless commerce' a decade ago. The language is deliberate: 'autonomous commerce systems sense signals, determine the right action, and carry it out.' They are pre-positioning for a market where AI agents execute commerce operations without human input. Where commercetools is now: claiming their API-native architecture makes them uniquely ready for AI agent workloads. Where they could go next: this reads as groundwork for positioning 'agent-readiness' as a competitive differentiator in enterprise deals, shifting the conversation from API flexibility to whether a platform can serve AI agents as first-class consumers.
competitor_cards.recommended_action: Audit your own positioning for AI agent use cases. Verify whether your APIs appear in AI coding agent training data or tool registries. If not, this is a gap commercetools will exploit.

theses.thesis: commercetools is conceding customer-facing AI ("agentic shopping") to competitors while staking claim to the higher-value "autonomous commerce" category, betting that enterprise AI infrastructure ownership matters more than the shopping assistant layer.
